content: Interactive graph editors in React degrade with node count unless the state and render path are disciplined. The React Flow performance docs name the causes: unnecessary re-renders from new function/object references on every render (memoize props with useCallback/useMemo and declare custom node/edge components outside the parent or wrap in React.memo), and components reading the whole nodes/edges array from the store (use granular selectors or keep selection in a separate store slice so an unrelated change does not re-render everything). A documented React Flow issue (xyflow#5674) shows the same with hard profiling numbers on a ~50-node graph: dragging one node produced 736 EdgeWrapper renders and 1472 EdgeAnchor renders per frame because internal wrappers subscribe to the whole store; the maintainer's answer is that the pattern is a user-side issue - if a node component reads the edges array, every node re-renders when any edge changes, and useNodeConnections/useNodesData are the correct hooks. The Synergy Codes benchmark quantifies it: with an inline anonymous onNodeClick prop, dragging 100 default nodes fell from 60 FPS to 10 FPS, and 100 'heavy' nodes to 2 FPS; wrapping custom node components in React.memo restored 50-60 FPS for default nodes and 30 FPS for heavy nodes. xyflow maintainers note 450 basic nodes are fine if usage is correct and advise onlyRenderVisibleElements for larger graphs; a separate discussion reports visible lag already around 100 nodes in a heavy use case and recommends a canvas renderer plus viewport culling. Canvas versus SVG benchmarks show canvas roughly 4-5x faster than SVG for the same graph. Practical thresholds for this project: a synthetic campus of 2-3 buildings x 3 floors with roughly 150-300 nodes and 200-400 edges is well inside the safe zone IF the editor keeps nodes/edges in a single store with granular selectors, memoizes callbacks and object props, memoizes custom node components, and avoids reading the whole array inside individual node components. A floor plan image backdrop must not be re-scaled by React on every state change; it should be a positioned layer under a transformed SVG/canvas edge layer.
